name: cards-v1
procedure:
Procedure (for any Newton simulation task):
1. Criteria. Copy every stated requirement into CHECKLIST.md: each metric with its threshold and window, every stated variation (unseen cases, perturbations, rates), every limit and constraint, and the command verification runs.
2. Check script. Write check.py. It runs the deliverable the way verification will (a fresh process with the stated command), covers the closest local analog of each stated variation, and prints one line per criterion (value, threshold, worst-case margin) plus the minutes left. Run it on the starting files: this is your baseline.
3. Diagnose before tuning. Name the symptom and find its card in the Debug Card index (for an error or warning message, card MSG-01). Run the card's checks before reading Newton source. Before using an unfamiliar API, check its signature (inspect.signature, help) instead of guessing.
4. Experiment. Change one cause at a time. The first time you use a way of editing the model, apply an extreme value and confirm that the output changes. Time one evaluation, then run variants side by side where you can (newton.utils.BatchRollout). Log one line per experiment in NOTES.md: the change and the worst margin.
5. Loop monitor. After three experiments in a row that do not improve the worst margin, stop sweeping: split the error into its parts, look for a shared cause, and re-read the matching card.
6. Save. When check.py passes every criterion, copy the deliverable files to pass_<n>/ before changing anything else.
7. Finish. When every criterion passes with a clear margin (about 20%) in a fresh-process run of the stated command, report and stop. If a margin is thin and more than a quarter of the time is left, work only on that criterion, re-run check.py after each change, and restore the saved copy if anything regresses.
Shell: run anything longer than a minute in the background with output to a file and its own timeout, and poll with short commands; stop processes by their PID, never by pattern; name scratch files dbg_*.py.

name: cards-v2
procedure:
Procedure (for any Newton simulation task):
1. Criteria. Copy every stated requirement into CHECKLIST.md: each metric with its threshold and window, every stated variation (unseen cases, perturbations, rates), every limit and constraint, and the command verification runs.
2. Measurement. Put the metric code in one module (metrics.py) that both your experiments and check.py import. Test it once on a case with a known answer (for example the reference compared with itself gives zero error) before trusting it.
3. Check script. check.py runs the deliverable the way verification will (a fresh process with the stated command), covers the closest local analog of each stated variation (if verification uses cases you cannot see, tune on part of your data and let check.py score the rest; cards FIT-05 and CTL-09), and prints one line per criterion (value, threshold, margin) plus the minutes left. Run it on the starting files: this is your baseline.
4. Diagnose before tuning. Name the symptom, find its card (for an error or warning message, card MSG-01), and run the card's checks before reading Newton source. Before using an unfamiliar API, check its signature (inspect.signature, help) instead of guessing.
5. Experiment quickly. Run experiments in-process (the live session if you have one, or one script that evaluates many variants, e.g. newton.utils.BatchRollout), not one fresh process per variant. Sweep the parameters you are allowed to change over a wide range (about 0.1x to 10x) before building new mechanisms. Change one cause at a time; the first time you use a way of editing the model, confirm with an extreme value that the output changes. Log one line per experiment in NOTES.md: the change and the worst margin. Differences smaller than the spread between your tuning and held-out scores are noise; do not tune them.
6. Loop monitor. After three experiments in a row that do not improve the worst margin, stop sweeping: split the error into its parts, look for a shared cause, and re-read the matching card.
7. Save. When your quick measurement passes every criterion, run check.py; if it passes, copy the deliverable files to pass_<n>/ before changing anything else.
8. Finish. When check.py passes every criterion with a clear margin (about 20%), report and stop; do not make cosmetic edits afterwards. If a margin is thin and more than a quarter of the time is left, work only on that criterion and restore the saved copy if anything regresses. While any criterion fails and more than a quarter of the time is left, do not finish: go back to step 4 with a different hypothesis and the cards you have not read yet.
Shell: run anything longer than a minute in the background with output to a file and its own timeout, and poll with short commands; stop processes by their PID, never by pattern; name scratch files dbg_*.py.

- BAT-05: Identical worlds or repeated runs disagree
- BLD-01: Hand-built body: mass properties are wrong, outside physical bounds, or not what you set
- BLD-02: Compound or mesh collider: seams, gaps, wrong radius, flipped faces
- BLD-03: Calibrated camera: projected points miss the photo, or pixel-to-world placement is off
- BLD-04: Camera render: a shape is missing, visibility edits change nothing, or colours are off by a gamma
- BLD-05: Geometry edits (SDF, mesh) do not reach collision or rendering; probing contacts at a pose
- CON-01: Contact parameters come from the other shape: priority, solmix and max rules
- CON-02: Contacts too soft, or stiffening does nothing: how shape ke/kd become MuJoCo solref
- CON-03: A firmly held object creeps slowly and no contact parameter moves it
- CON-04: Held object rotates or slips during motion: friction cone and impratio
- CON-05: Torsional or rolling friction does nothing; released objects keep rolling
- CON-06: Expected contacts are missing: objects pass through, fall through, launch, or one world misbehaves
- CON-07: Contact force readouts are zero or implausible, or raw contact rows mislead
- CON-08: Fingers close past the object with almost no force: the grasp never forms
- CON-09: Grip force or finger gap is wrong: the force limit never binds, or the finger-mirror equality yields
- CON-10: A negative control holds: the object lifts with near-zero friction or an open gripper
- CON-11: Some worlds go NaN or explode
- CTL-01: Servo gain or target edits have no, partial or unexpected effect
- CTL-02: Floating-base robot sags, sways and falls under joint-PD tracking; feedforward is fought by the servo
- CTL-03: Joints track the reference but the robot tips or its feet spin: the reference is not dynamically feasible
- CTL-04: A feedback channel destabilizes as soon as it is enabled, or integral action makes standing worse
- CTL-05: Hand-written IK or Jacobian diverges, blows up, or returns zeros
- CTL-06: Newton vs MuJoCo state conventions and names break a planner, estimator or feedback law
- CTL-07: Planner or private-model predictions diverge from the plant within one control period
- CTL-08: Controller holds a stance but fails at support changes, landings, or late in a cyclic motion
- CTL-09: Controller passes its own runs but fails a repeated, held-out or loaded run
- FIT-01: Identification fit is inconsistent or negative, or many parameter sets fit equally well
- FIT-02: Error plateaus at the same value under every variant: residual floor, missing mechanism, or reference bias
- FIT-03: Replayed robot misses the recording: latency, gravity sag and servo gains
- FIT-04: Impacts, slides and rest poses do not match recordings
